sections.context: DockerfileSource (image.dockerfile, inline or path) is consumed only by the Daytona provider (snapshot build + dockerfile_sha256 cache key in daytona/snapshot_identity). The Docker provider accepts only image.docker (a finished image) and ignores image.dockerfile with a warning (docs/public/execution/environments.mdx provider matrix). Repos that run docker sandboxes must bake runner images outside fabro (manual docker build or external CI), or pay per-run toolchain setup: in the denkhaus lab, mise install costs ~24.5s of every ~32s run setup (run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0, events seq 13-14). Runner-image-as-config should travel with the repo for docker exactly like it already does for daytona.
sections.approach: Mirror the daytona caching discipline inside the docker sandbox layer. Code path: fabro-types EnvironmentImageSettings.dockerfile -> run_compiler resolves Path refs to Inline from bundled files (already implemented for daytona, resolve_dockerfile) -> fabro-sandbox::from_environment::docker_config_from_environment_env maps the inline dockerfile into DockerSandboxOptions (new field, inline-only like DaytonaSnapshotSettings.dockerfile) -> DockerSandbox::ensure_image gains a build branch: derive tag fabro-runner-<sha12> from the inline content (same sha256 identity idea as daytona::snapshot_identity, but no API key/tenant scope), inspect_image first; on hit reuse without rebuild, on miss build via bollard build_image with a minimal tar context containing only the Dockerfile, label the image with the fabro managed label, emit the existing SnapshotCreating/SnapshotReady/SnapshotFailed sandbox events (no new event variants needed; snapshot == image source), and surface build stream errors through crate::Error. Validation in fabro-config/resolve/environment.rs: docker provider setting both image.docker and image.dockerfile becomes a resolve error (ambiguous), symmetric to the existing daytona+image.docker error; a Path dockerfile reaching the sandbox layer is an error, matching the daytona invariant. Both entry paths (fabro-workflow operations/start.rs via docker_config_from_environment_with_secrets and fabro-server run_manifest.rs via docker_config_from_environment) flow through the same mapping, so one change covers CLI and server workers.

alternatives.name: Build during server preflight instead of sandbox initialize
alternatives.rejected_because: Preflight runs without a vault and duplicates daemon access; ensure_image in initialize() is the single choke point both the CLI run path and server workers already use, and it already implements pull-if-missing semantics the build branch can mirror.

alternatives.name: Persist the built image reference in the environment store
alternatives.rejected_because: The content-hash tag is self-describing and stateless, exactly like the daytona snapshot name derivation; no new stored state to migrate or invalidate.

alternatives.name: Keep image.docker + documented manual build script
alternatives.rejected_because: That is the status quo the seed removes; runner-image-as-config should travel with the repo.

alternatives.name: Full build-context support (COPY bundled files)
alternatives.rejected_because: Inline/path dockerfiles build with an empty context, same constraint daytona snapshots have; a context-bearing form needs manifest archive semantics and is a separate feature.

steps.title: Config plumbing: map image.dockerfile into DockerSandboxOptions and validate provider rules
steps.description: 1) Add an inline-only dockerfile build source to DockerSandboxOptions in fabro-sandbox/src/docker.rs (Option<String> or a small DockerfileSource reuse from crate::config; reject/never construct Path there). 2) Extend from_environment.rs docker_config_from_environment_env: when settings.image.dockerfile is Some and image.docker is None, carry the inline content into the options; keep the buildpack-deps:noble default when neither is set. 3) fabro-config resolve/environment.rs: new validation error when provider=docker sets both image.docker and image.dockerfile (ambiguous image source), next to the existing daytona rule; docs/public/execution/environments.mdx matrix cell changes from 'Warning; ignored' in the docs step. 4) Unit tests: fabro-config resolve tests for the both-set error and dockerfile-only acceptance; from_environment mapping tests (dockerfile-only, neither, secrets path unchanged). Files: lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/docker.rs, lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/from_environment.rs, lib/foundation/fabro-config/src/resolve/environment.rs, lib/foundation/fabro-config/src/tests/resolve_run.rs.

steps.title: Core: ensure_image builds fabro-runner-<sha12> on first use and reuses on content-hash hit
steps.description: 1) Tag derivation helper (sha256 of inline dockerfile, hex, first 12 chars, prefix fabro-runner-) in fabro-sandbox, unit-tested; keep it pure so manifest-stored options stay deterministic. 2) DockerSandbox::ensure_image: when the build source is set, resolve config.image to the derived tag; inspect_image hit -> AlreadyLocal (no rebuild, no build events); miss -> emit SnapshotCreating{name}, bollard build_image with BuildImageOptions{dockerfile, labels incl. sh.fabro.managed, t: tag} over a tar archive containing only the Dockerfile (tar crate is already a docker-feature dep, see archive code near docker.rs:334), consume the BuildInfo stream collecting 'error' entries into crate::Error context so failures read as clear sandbox errors, then emit SnapshotReady/SnapshotFailed. Respect auto_pull=false as skip-build. 3) The existing bash/git requirement check (DOCKER_BASH_REQUIREMENT) keeps guarding unsuitable dockerfiles after start. 4) Tests: unit tests for tag derivation and tar context layout; an #[ignore]d real-daemon test beside tests/docker_streaming.rs that builds a trivial dockerfile twice and asserts the second initialize emits no build events, plus a changed-content case that produces a new tag. Files: lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/docker.rs, lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/sandbox.rs (only if event mapping needs it), lib/components/fabro-sandbox/tests/.

steps.title: Docs and lab validation: environments.mdx, run-configuration.mdx, mise runner example
steps.description: 1) docs/public/execution/environments.mdx: provider matrix row image.dockerfile for Docker becomes 'Auto-built image tagged fabro-runner-<sha12>; reused while content hash matches'; document the empty build context (no COPY), the both-set error, and failure surfacing in the Docker section; add an inline + { path } example. 2) docs/public/execution/run-configuration.mdx field table row for image.dockerfile: replace the daytona-only wording with both providers. 3) Validate end-to-end in the denkhaus lab with the mise runner dockerfile that motivated the seed: a run using image.dockerfile with mise preinstalled must skip the ~24.5s per-run mise install; link the lab run id and the example in seed fabro-969f before closing it. 4) Note the follow-up in the seed or a new seed: prune/GC of labeled fabro-runner-* images (system prune currently does not touch images).

risks: bollard build_image reports failures inside the BuildInfo stream ('error' field), not always as transport errors; if not collected explicitly, root causes vanish and users see a generic failure. Mitigate by folding stream error text into the crate::Error context, mirroring how create_image pull errors are wrapped today.

Inline-only, empty build context means COPY/ADD cannot reference repo files; dockerfiles that need repo files will fail at build with a docker-native error. Document the limitation and the error path rather than inventing context semantics.

A Path dockerfile reaching the sandbox layer un-inlined (future callers bypassing run_compiler) must fail loudly like daytona snapshot_identity does, otherwise builds silently diverge from the repo file.

First-use builds can take minutes on a cold daemon and block sandbox initialize; SnapshotCreating/Ready events keep progress visible, but run setup duration metrics will shift - acceptable, that is the trade the feature makes.

Content-hash-only tags are shared across projects on the same daemon: identical dockerfiles intentionally share one image; divergent dockerfiles accumulate images. Labeling enables later GC; pruning stays out of scope here.
acceptance: image.dockerfile works for provider=docker in both forms: inline string and { path = ... } resolved from bundled workflow files

The image is built once per content hash: tag is fabro-runner-<sha12> of the dockerfile content, and an unchanged dockerfile produces no rebuild on subsequent runs (verified via sandbox events / inspect_image reuse)
Setting both image.docker and image.dockerfile on a docker environment fails config resolution with a clear error; setting neither keeps today's default image
Build failures surface as clear sandbox/preflight errors including the docker build error output
docs/public/execution/environments.mdx and run-configuration.mdx document the field, the caching behavior, the empty build context, and the both-set rule
A lab-validated example (denkhaus lab mise runner) with its run id is linked in seed fabro-969f
cargo nextest run -p fabro-sandbox -p fabro-config passes; real-daemon build/reuse test included behind the existing ignore convention
